newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebels order Hutu refugees to leave camp.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels order Hutu refugees to leave camp.

text.p: About 20,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees stranded in eastern Zaire after a four-month trek through the jungle have been ordered to leave a temporary camp close to Kisangani on Sunday, the U.N. refugee agency said.
Rebels who seized Zaire's third city two weeks ago said the refugees at Lula seven km (four miles) south of Kisangani must move back from the city towards a site 25 km (15 miles) to the south.
The decision to close the camp was disclosed a day after Zaire rebels denied the United Nations World Food Programme access to Lula to bring food.
"The big issue today is that we have to relocate Lula camp and that is a big problem," Kilian Kleinschmidt of the Office of the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) said on Sunday.
"They have to move today, otherwise there is a risk they could be pushed back by the military," Kleinschmidt said in a telephone interview from Kisangani.
Aid agencies said on Saturday that thousands of refugees trapped in the Zaire jungle near a railway line could die unless aid workers provided food, water and medicine.
At least 500 refugees have died since arriving at the village of Ubilo 82 km (51 miles) south of the city on March 16, according to the Zairean Red Cross.

Rebels from the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo (ADFL) have seized control of about a quarter of the country since last October in a war to oust ailing President Mobutu Sese Seko.
Negotiations between the ADFL and envoys of Mobutu could start early this week, probably in South Africa, according to an Alliance spokesman.

Aid agencies sent a trainload of medical supplies and provisions such as soap and blankets on Sunday to up to 40,000 Rwandan Hutus gathered at a point 41 km (25 miles) south of Kisangani, Kleinschmidt said.
The strongest refugees are gradually moving north towards Kisangani along the railway line that runs through dense jungle.
Rebels have killed about 100 armed refugees in clashes since taking Kisangani, according to Red Cross officials.

Senior ADFL officials say members of the former Rwandan government army (FAR) and Interahamwe militia among the refugees pose a military threat, while the refugees themselves distract attention from impoverished and displaced Zaireans.
More than a million Hutus fled camps on the Rwandan and Burundian border last October and November at the start of a campaign by rebels fighting the Zairean army.

About 600,000 returned to Rwanda in November via Goma, but hundreds of thousands more fled west into the jungle, including former Rwandan army troops and Interahamwe held responsible for massacres during the 1994 genocide in Rwanda.
Since then the refugees -- now begging to return home -- have set up a series of makeshift camps and fled before the rebel advance in a trek that has hampered relief efforts.

UNHCR said it was appealing to donors for money to fly the most vulnerable refugees direct to the Rwandan capital Kigali from Kisangani at a rate of up to 2,000 per day. The rest, once they were strong enough, could then return to Rwanda overland by truck, barge and on foot.
